title: Sampling Alignment Gateway and Mutable Context Patcher for SDK Instrumentation
creator: Samira Patel
description: Implement a lightweight gateway inside our SDKs and middleware that aligns sampling decisions across heterogeneous carriers and downstream proxies, plus a small, runtime-safe 'mutable context patcher' to reconcile legacy header shapes. Goal: eliminate duplicate traces from inconsistent sampling headers and prevent context drift when requests traverse mixed ecosystems (old proxies, third-party sidecars, Redwood edge). The gateway should: 1) canonicalize incoming sampling headers into a single internal decision token, 2) surface a stable outbound header pattern that downstream Redwood services and external partners can read, and 3) expose hooks for policy overrides (sampling ratio, sticky-sampling per-customer) via local config. The mutable context patcher is a minimal, deterministic transformer that can add/normalize span ids and baggage keys without breaking existing integrations. Must be safe for high-concurrency runtimes (Node, Go, Python), zero allocations on hot paths where possible, and feature-flag controlled so we can roll back quickly.
acceptance_criteria: Canonicalization: SDK converts at least 6 known vendor header formats into a single internal sampling token with tests
Interop: Outbound headers are accepted by Redwood runtime routing and result in single linked trace for cross-service calls in staging
Performance: End-to-end median latency impact of SDK instrumentation < 150 microseconds on Node baseline in our benchmark harness
Safety: Mutable context patcher has deterministic behavior and passes concurrency fuzz tests for span id collisions
Rollout: Feature flag implemented and can be toggled per-route from Console; rollout plan documented in Confluence
comments: 2026-01-18 - Samira Patel: Initial ticket created after postmortem for INC-2026-01. Root cause: multiple proxies setting different sampling headers leading to duplicated root spans and overcounting in latency dashboards.

2026-01-21 - Liam Chen: Spike finished. Implemented prototype canonicalizer for three header formats and verified single trace linkage in local microbench with envoy sidecar. Observed extra 90us on hot path in Node; need micro-optimizations.

2026-01-25 - Priya Nair (code review): Left feedback on concurrency model for Go SDK patcher. Suggested using object pooling and pointer arenas to reduce allocations. Also called out need for deterministic unit tests for header precedence.
2026-01-28 - Data Eng (Nico Alvarez): We should expose a debug endpoint that shows sampling decisions and provenance per-request for first-party customers; useful for triage. Added as docs task.

2026-02-02 - Liam Chen: Implemented feature flagging and Console toggle hook. Added e2e test that runs against staging cluster with mixed-version proxies. Ready for in-review PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/4821
notes: Trade-offs: we avoid creating a new wire header; instead we normalize to an existing, documented pattern to reduce partner upgrades. If customers require full fidelity of original vendor headers we will include them in a debug-only metadata bag (not guaranteed for sampling). Rollout plan: gated by feature flag and staged to 10% of traffic, then 50%, then 100% after 72h of monitoring for duplication regressions. Monitoring: add an alert if duplicate-root-span-rate > 0.1% above baseline.
